description: Make the monster's AI chat reply in the selected language by threading a lang flag end-to-end: add an optional lang?: 'ja'|'en' to the ChatRequest DTO (default 'ja' when absent for backward compatibility), pass it from the frontend (useMonster.sendChat -> api.chat), branch the Bedrock system prompt wording and the 'reply in {language}' instruction in backend chat.ts on it, and give the baby canned non-verbal reply an EN variant selected by lang (both the backend chat.ts baby branch AND, already done in FEAT-001, the frontend mirror). The user said chat-AI language is desirable; UI strings are the floor and are covered by FEAT-001/002. Changing chat.ts REQUIRES an AWS redeploy, which the ORCHESTRATOR performs after merge; the coder must NOT run cdk deploy. Keep the default 'ja' so already-deployed backends and old clients behave exactly as today. Depends on FEAT-001 (Lang type, babySpeechText) and should be consistent with FEAT-002's lang wiring.
steps: In packages/shared/src/types.ts: add `lang?: 'ja' | 'en';` to the ChatRequest interface (optional, documented as defaulting to 'ja' when absent). Optionally export a shared `export type Lang = 'ja' | 'en';` and reuse it, but do not break the frontend's own Lang in i18n.ts (they can be structurally identical). Rebuild shared (`npm run build -w @ddm/shared`).

In packages/backend/src/handlers/chat.ts: read lang from the parsed body with a safe default: `const lang = body.lang === 'en' ? 'en' : 'ja';`. Branch buildSystemPrompt on lang: for 'ja' keep the current Japanese prompt BYTE-IDENTICAL (same 6 lines) so JA behavior is unchanged; for 'en' produce an English system prompt conveying the same intent (you are a digital monster named {name}; current growth stage {labelEn}; chat briefly and friendly with the owner; monster-like, innocent, energetic persona; higher stages are smarter/calmer; reply in English in 2-3 short sentences). Use the stage's labelEn (added in FEAT-001) for the English stage name. Pass lang into buildSystemPrompt (e.g. buildSystemPrompt(context, lang)).

In packages/backend/src/handlers/chat.ts baby branch: when stage cannot chat, return the JA canned reply '…！（まだ言葉を話せないみたい。もっと育ててあげよう！）' when lang!=='en' (BYTE-IDENTICAL to today) and an English canned non-verbal reply when lang==='en' (e.g. '…! (It can\'t speak yet. Raise it a bit more!)') that mirrors the frontend BABY_SPEECH_TEXT_EN from FEAT-001. Keep modelId 'none'. Also localize the two fallback strings ('…（うまく返事ができなかったみたい）' and the empty-reply fallback) by lang so an EN session never shows a stray Japanese fallback.

In packages/frontend/src/api.ts: no signature change needed if chat() already forwards the whole ChatRequest; confirm it serializes the new optional lang field (it does, since it JSON.stringifies the request). If chat() constructs a narrowed object, include lang.

In packages/frontend/src/state/useMonster.ts: sendChat currently builds the api.chat({...}) payload. Thread the current UI language into it. Since useMonster is a hook, obtain lang from the I18nProvider (either call useI18n() inside useMonster, or accept lang as a parameter to sendChat / to the hook). Simplest: have sendChat accept the current lang, or read it from useI18n() at the top of useMonster. Pass lang into api.chat so the backend replies in the selected language. Ensure the frontend baby bubble (handled in App via babySpeechText(lang)) and this lang stay consistent.

Confirm the backend still compiles and the whole monorepo builds. Do NOT deploy. Make sure that when lang is absent/‘ja’, the produced system prompt and canned replies are byte-identical to the pre-change behavior (compare against the original 6-line prompt and the exact JA canned string).

If feasible without heavy mocking, add a tiny pure test for the lang-selected baby canned reply at the frontend layer (already covered by babySpeechText tests in FEAT-001) and note in findings that the backend prompt branching is covered by build + manual reasoning (backend has no unit test harness today; do not add a new test framework).
acceptance_criteria: ChatRequest in packages/shared/src/types.ts has an optional lang?: 'ja'|'en'; shared rebuilds cleanly.

backend chat.ts reads lang (default 'ja'), builds a Japanese prompt byte-identical to today when lang!=='en', and an English prompt instructing an English reply when lang==='en'; the baby canned reply and fallback strings are JA by default and EN when lang==='en'; modelId behavior unchanged.
Frontend threads the active UI language into api.chat via useMonster.sendChat, so selecting EN makes the monster reply in English after redeploy.
Default-'ja' backward compatibility: with no lang (old clients) the backend output is identical to the current deployed behavior.
`npm run build` from repo root exits 0; the coder did NOT run cdk deploy.
verification: From repo root: `npm run build` exits 0 (shared -> backend -> frontend -> infra).
From repo root: `npm test` (shared, >=47 pass, 0 fail) and the frontend ui-helpers runner pass with 0 failures.
Inspect chat.ts: confirm the lang==='ja'/absent branch reproduces the original 6-line Japanese system prompt and the exact JA canned reply string character-for-character.
